# SPDX-License-Identifier: FSL-1.1-ALv2
#
# API connector adapter for the fixture CRM (server.ts in this directory).
# Written by following .claude/skills/api-connector-authoring/SKILL.md from
# the fixture's openapi.json. It fills all six roles plus three writes
# (a company note, a new company, a new contact).
#
# baseUrl is the fixture's default local address. A loopback http baseUrl is
# accepted by the schema, but the connector only reaches it when the
# deployment sets LIAISON_ALLOW_PRIVATE_API_CONNECTOR_HOSTS=true (development
# only); a real API uses https.
$schema: ../../../../../../../packages/api-connector-core/adapter.schema.json
id: fixture-crm
name: Fixture CRM
version: "1.0.0"
description: A small fictional CRM/ERP (companies, contacts, deals, orders, invoices, stock).
baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:4010/v1
auth:
  type: apiKey
  in: header
  name: X-Api-Key
operations:
  - name: find_customers
    description: >-
      Find customer companies by a contact's email address, a contact's phone
      number, or the company's email domain (e.g. acme-instruments.example).
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /companies
    role: customer.lookup
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        email: { type: string, format: email, description: A contact's email address }
        phone: { type: string, maxLength: 40, description: A contact's phone number }
        domain: { type: string, maxLength: 253, description: The company's email domain }
    query:
      email: "{email}"
      phone: "{phone}"
      domain: "{domain}"
    items: /data
    fields: [id, name, domain, city, country, tier]

  - name: list_companies
    description: List customer companies, optionally filtered by a name fragment.
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /companies
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        q: { type: string, maxLength: 100, description: Part of the company name }
        limit: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, description: Page size }
    query:
      q: "{q}"
      limit: "{limit}"
    items: /data
    pagination:
      type: cursor
      param: cursor
      cursorPointer: /next_cursor
    fields: [id, name, domain, industry, country, tier]

  - name: get_customer_summary
    description: >-
      One customer company's summary: location, tier, account manager,
      lifetime value, open balance and last order date.
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /companies/{customerId}
    role: customer.summary
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        customerId: { type: string, maxLength: 64, description: The company id (cmp_...) }
      required: [customerId]
    items: /company
    fields:
      - id
      - name
      - domain
      - industry
      - city
      - country
      - tier
      - currency
      - account_manager.name
      - account_manager.email
      - contacts_count
      - open_deals
      - lifetime_value
      - open_balance
      - last_order_date

  - name: list_contacts
    description: The people at one customer company.
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /companies/{customerId}/contacts
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        customerId: { type: string, maxLength: 64 }
      required: [customerId]
    items: /data
    fields: [id, first_name, last_name, email, phone, title]

  - name: list_orders
    description: >-
      One customer's sales orders, newest first, with their lines. Use since
      (YYYY-MM-DD) to restrict to orders placed on or after a date.
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /companies/{customerId}/orders
    role: customer.orders
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        customerId: { type: string, maxLength: 64 }
        since: { type: string, format: date, description: Earliest order date (YYYY-MM-DD) }
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [pending, shipped, delivered, cancelled]
      required: [customerId]
    query:
      since: "{since}"
      status: "{status}"
    items: /data
    fields:
      - id
      - number
      - date
      - status
      - currency
      - total
      - lines.sku
      - lines.description
      - lines.quantity
      - lines.unit_price

  - name: list_recent_orders
    description: >-
      The latest sales orders across every customer, newest first, each with
      its company's id and name and its lines. Use it to find the most recent
      customer or what was ordered lately; no customer id needed.
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /orders
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        limit: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 100, description: How many orders (default 25) }
        since: { type: string, format: date, description: Earliest order date (YYYY-MM-DD) }
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [pending, shipped, delivered, cancelled]
    query:
      limit: "{limit}"
      since: "{since}"
      status: "{status}"
    items: /data
    fields:
      - id
      - number
      - date
      - company_id
      - company_name
      - status
      - currency
      - total
      - lines.sku
      - lines.description
      - lines.quantity
      - lines.unit_price

  - name: list_invoices
    description: One customer's invoices, optionally filtered by status.
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /companies/{customerId}/invoices
    role: customer.invoices
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        customerId: { type: string, maxLength: 64 }
        status: { type: string, enum: [paid, open, overdue] }
      required: [customerId]
    query:
      status: "{status}"
    items: /data
    fields: [id, number, order_id, issued_on, due_on, status, total, currency]

  - name: list_deals
    description: One customer's sales opportunities (deals) and their stage.
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /companies/{customerId}/deals
    role: deal.list
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        customerId: { type: string, maxLength: 64 }
        stage: { type: string, enum: [lead, qualified, proposal, won, lost] }
      required: [customerId]
    query:
      stage: "{stage}"
    items: /data
    fields: [id, title, stage, amount, currency, probability, expected_close, owner.name]

  - name: check_stock
    description: Stock levels per product, by exact sku or a product-name search.
    kind: read
    method: GET
    path: /stock
    role: stock.check
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        sku: { type: string, maxLength: 64, description: Exact product sku (e.g. OSC-200) }
        query: { type: string, maxLength: 100, description: Part of the product name }
    query:
      sku: "{sku}"
      q: "{query}"
    items: /data
    fields: [sku, name, warehouse, on_hand, reserved, available, restock_date]

  - name: create_note
    description: Add a note to a customer company's timeline (visible to the CRM's users).
    kind: write
    method: POST
    path: /companies/{customerId}/notes
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        customerId: { type: string, maxLength: 64 }
        text: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 2000, description: The note text }
        pinned: { type: boolean, description: Pin the note at the top of the timeline }
      required: [customerId, text]
    body:
      note:
        body: "{text}"
        pinned: "{pinned}"
    items: /note
    fields: [id, company_id, body, pinned, created_at]

  - name: create_company
    description: >-
      Create a customer company. Look it up first (find_customers by domain,
      list_companies by name): a domain that already exists is refused.
    kind: write
    method: POST
    path: /companies
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        name: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 200, description: The company name }
        domain: { type: string, maxLength: 253, description: "The company's email or web domain (e.g. acme-instruments.example)" }
        industry: { type: string, maxLength: 200 }
        city: { type: string, maxLength: 200 }
        country: { type: string, maxLength: 2, description: ISO country code (e.g. FR) }
      required: [name]
    body:
      company:
        name: "{name}"
        domain: "{domain}"
        industry: "{industry}"
        city: "{city}"
        country: "{country}"
    items: /company
    fields: [id, name, domain, industry, city, country]

  - name: create_contact
    description: >-
      Create a person at a customer company: give customerId for a company the
      CRM already has, or companyName (and companyDomain) to create the company
      in the same call. An email that already exists is refused.
    kind: write
    method: POST
    path: /contacts
    params:
      type: object
      properties:
        email: { type: string, format: email, description: "The person's email address" }
        firstName: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 200 }
        lastName: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 200 }
        title: { type: string, maxLength: 200, description: Their job title }
        phone: { type: string, maxLength: 40 }
        customerId: { type: string, maxLength: 64, description: An existing company id (cmp_...) }
        companyName: { type: string, maxLength: 200, description: "A new company's name, when the CRM has none" }
        companyDomain: { type: string, maxLength: 253, description: "The new company's domain" }
        companyIndustry: { type: string, maxLength: 200, description: "What the new company does, in a short line" }
      required: [email, firstName, lastName]
    body:
      contact:
        first_name: "{firstName}"
        last_name: "{lastName}"
        email: "{email}"
        title: "{title}"
        phone: "{phone}"
        company_id: "{customerId}"
        company:
          $when: companyName
          name: "{companyName}"
          domain: "{companyDomain}"
          industry: "{companyIndustry}"
    items: /contact
    fields: [id, company_id, first_name, last_name, email, title]
